verdict_reason: Organisation scoping is complete and correct on every read and write, and the PUT hand-copy misses no field today, but the copy has no compile-time guard, phone is untested on the PUT path, and the list timer's name defeats the EMF publisher's meter reset.

todos.issue: update() hand-copies the nine client fields with setters instead of a MapStruct @MappingTarget method, so the mapper's unmappedTargetPolicy=ERROR guard (which protects toEntity/toResponse) does not cover the PUT path: add a field to AddressRequest+Address and toEntity fails the build while update() silently keeps compiling and PUT retains stale data for the new field.
todos.fix: Add 'void updateEntity(AddressRequest request, @MappingTarget Address address)' to OperatorMapper with the same @Mapping(ignore) set for id/organisationId/status/createdAt/modifiedAt and ignoreUnmappedSourceProperties {type, role}, and call it from update() in place of the nine setters, so a future field addition is a compile-time failure rather than a silent stale-data bug.

todos.issue: The PUT full-replace of 'phone' is asserted nowhere: OperatorServiceTest.updateAppliesTheNewFieldValues... checks name/addressLine1/townOrCity/postcode/email only, AddressUpdateIT.putReplacesAllFieldsAndClearsOmittedOptionals checks name plus the cleared addressLine2/county, and OperatorCrudIT checks name/addressLine1/townOrCity/countryCode - so deleting 'existing.setPhone(request.phone())' leaves the stale telephone number on the document and the whole suite still passes.
todos.fix: Assert the replaced phone value in OperatorServiceTest.updateAppliesTheNewFieldValuesBumpsModifiedAtAndPreservesTheServerOwnedFields (assertThat(updated.getPhone()).isEqualTo("+44 1738 111222")) and in AddressUpdateIT.putReplacesAllFieldsAndClearsOmittedOptionals, and while there add the missing addressLine2 set-to-a-new-value case so every one of the nine replaced fields has at least one assertion.

todos.issue: The list timer is registered as 'OperatorListQuery' - PascalCase, breaking the dot-delimited Micrometer convention used everywhere else in the service ('controller.listOperators.time', best-practice 'notification.save'), and more importantly EmfMetricsPublisher.publishMetrics() only removes meters whose name startsWith("controller"), so this meter is never reset and its cumulative COUNT and TOTAL_TIME are re-emitted to CloudWatch on every 60s publish cycle - the metric grows monotonically instead of reporting the interval's activity.
todos.fix: Rename the timer to a dot-delimited, controller-prefix-consistent name that EmfMetricsPublisher's reset filter picks up (e.g. meterRegistry.timer("controller.listOperators.query.time")), or widen the reset filter in EmfMetricsPublisher to cover service meters; also wrap the query in try/finally so the sample is stopped when queryPage throws.
